summary: The upgrade from Ubuntu 18.04 to 20.04 will involve several package updates and new features, including cloud-init, PHP, Python, and network configuration improvements. Users should be aware of potential known issues and the removal of Python 2 support.

claims.text: The upgrade process for Ubuntu 18.04 to 20.04 will include an update to cloud-init to version 20.1-10, which includes notable features such as improved configuration file handling.
Users will see an upgrade to PHP 7.4, bringing new features like typed properties and arrow functions, while Python 3.8.2 becomes the default version.
The upgrade process will also involve the removal of Python 2 support, with /usr/bin/python pointing to python2 for compatibility on newly-installed systems.
Known issues include some significant bugs that users may encounter, as documented in the release notes for Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.
The upgrade from Ubuntu 18.04 to 20.04 will include a refreshed toolchain with new upstream releases of glibc, OpenJDK, rustc, GCC, Python, Ruby, PHP, and Perl.
Network configuration improvements in Ubuntu 20.04 LTS include basic support for configuring SR-IOV network devices and adding WiFi flags for bssid, band, and channel settings.
Users should ensure they have a network connection to an official mirror or locally accessible mirror for the upgrade process, as there are no offline options.
